quizzes.title: Carbon Footprint & Environmental Impact
quizzes.description: Learn about carbon footprints and how to reduce your environmental impact
quizzes.author: e-icon World Contest

questions.question: What is a carbon footprint?

answers.text: The size of a person's shoe
The total amount of carbon dioxide emitted by a person, group, or activity
The black residue from burnt coal

questions.explanation: A carbon footprint measures the total greenhouse gas emissions caused directly or indirectly by an individual, event, organization, or product.

questions.question: Which activity increases your carbon footprint the most?
questions.explanation: Air travel, especially long flights, generates significant emissions per passenger, making it one of the highest carbon-impact activities.

questions.question: What type of diet generally has the lowest carbon footprint?
questions.explanation: Plant-based diets reduce emissions because growing plants typically uses fewer resources and produces less greenhouse gas than raising animals.

questions.question: How can you reduce your carbon footprint at home?
questions.explanation: Solar panels generate clean energy from sunlight, reducing the need for fossil fuels and lowering household carbon emissions.

questions.question: Why is public transportation better for the environment than driving alone?

answers.text: It reduces the number of vehicles and emissions per person

questions.explanation: Public transport carries many passengers at once, significantly reducing emissions per person compared to private cars.

questions.question: What is a major benefit of buying local products?
questions.explanation: Locally produced goods travel shorter distances, cutting down on emissions from transportation like ships, trucks, or planes.

questions.question: Which of these helps reduce your digital carbon footprint?
questions.explanation: Digital activities use energy, especially servers and data centers. Reducing device usage and data storage helps cut emissions.

questions.question: How does energy efficiency help the planet?

answers.text: It reduces wasted energy and emissions

questions.explanation: Energy-efficient appliances and systems use less energy to perform the same tasks, helping reduce overall demand and emissions.

questions.question: Which is the most eco-friendly mode of transport for short distances?
questions.explanation: Electric scooters are emission-free during use and are ideal for short trips, helping reduce fossil fuel reliance.

questions.question: What does "carbon offsetting" mean?

answers.text: Funding projects that reduce emissions elsewhere

questions.explanation: Carbon offsetting compensates for your emissions by supporting projects like tree planting or renewable energy, balancing your impact.

quizzes.title: Climate Change Causes & Human Impact
quizzes.description: Explore the various causes of climate change and human impact on the environment
quizzes.author: e-icon World Contest

questions.question: What is the main cause of current climate change?

answers.text: Human activities like burning fossil fuels

questions.explanation: Human activities, especially burning fossil fuels, are the primary driver of today's rapid climate change.

questions.question: Which gas is the most emitted greenhouse gas by human activities?
questions.explanation: Carbon dioxide (CO₂) is the most emitted greenhouse gas, mainly from burning fossil fuels.

questions.question: What is a key contributor to deforestation?
questions.explanation: Large-scale agriculture drives deforestation by clearing forests for crops or livestock.

questions.question: Which sector is the largest source of greenhouse gas emissions?
questions.explanation: Energy production (mainly fossil fuel burning) is the largest contributor to global emissions.

questions.question: What human activity leads to ocean acidification?
questions.explanation: CO₂ dissolves into oceans, lowering pH and harming marine life—a process called ocean acidification.

questions.question: How does transportation affect the climate?

answers.text: It releases large amounts of greenhouse gases

questions.explanation: Cars, planes, and ships run on fossil fuels, emitting CO₂ and other warming gases.

questions.question: What impact does meat production have on climate?
questions.explanation: Livestock farming produces methane, a potent greenhouse gas, especially from cows.

questions.question: Which industry is responsible for significant industrial pollution?
questions.explanation: The chemical industry emits large amounts of GHGs and harmful pollutants during production.

questions.question: What happens when forests are cleared?
questions.explanation: Trees store carbon. When cut or burned, they release CO₂, accelerating climate change.

questions.question: Which is a direct human impact on biodiversity due to climate change?
questions.explanation: Warming, habitat destruction, and changing ecosystems threaten countless species worldwide.

quizzes.title: Climate Change Fundamentals
quizzes.description: Learn about the fundamentals of climate change and its impact on our planet
quizzes.author: e-icon World Contest

questions.question: What is climate change?

answers.text: Long-term change in global climate patterns

questions.explanation: Climate change refers to long-term alterations in temperature and weather patterns over decades.

questions.question: What causes the greenhouse effect?

answers.text: Gases like CO₂ and methane trapping heat

questions.explanation: Greenhouse gases trap heat in the atmosphere, keeping Earth warm—but excess causes warming.

questions.question: Which is a natural greenhouse gas?
questions.explanation: Methane occurs naturally and through human activities like agriculture and fossil fuel use.

questions.question: Which layer of the Earth is directly impacted by global warming?
questions.explanation: The atmosphere absorbs greenhouse gases and heat, leading to warming effects.

questions.question: Which region is most sensitive to climate change?
questions.explanation: Polar regions warm faster due to ice melt and feedback effects, disrupting global climate.

questions.question: What is one result of glacier melting?
questions.explanation: As glaciers melt, the water adds to the ocean volume, raising sea levels globally.

questions.question: What is a climate model?

answers.text: A computer simulation of Earth's climate

questions.explanation: Scientists use models to simulate and predict future climate scenarios using data.

questions.question: Which of the following is a sign of climate change?
questions.explanation: The reduction of Arctic and Antarctic ice is a direct result of warming temperatures.

questions.question: Which natural disaster is not directly linked to climate change?
questions.explanation: Earthquakes are geological events, not climate-related.

questions.question: Why are extreme weather events increasing?

answers.text: Warmer oceans and atmosphere intensify storms

questions.explanation: A warmer climate means more evaporation, energy, and intensity for storms and heatwaves.

quizzes.title: Renewable Energy Technologies
quizzes.description: Test your knowledge about solar, wind, hydroelectric, and other renewable energy technologies
quizzes.author: e-icon World Contest

questions.question: Which is a renewable energy source?
questions.explanation: Wind is clean and renewable—it doesn't deplete over time or emit greenhouse gases.

questions.question: What do solar panels convert sunlight into?
questions.explanation: Solar panels use photovoltaic cells to convert sunlight into usable electrical energy.

questions.question: Which device captures wind energy?
questions.explanation: Wind turbines use blades and generators to turn wind into electricity.

questions.question: What is the main requirement for hydroelectric power?
questions.explanation: Hydropower depends on moving water, such as rivers or dams, to generate electricity.

questions.question: Which energy source releases the most carbon dioxide?
questions.explanation: Coal is the dirtiest fossil fuel, emitting the highest CO₂ per unit of energy.

questions.question: What is geothermal energy?
questions.explanation: Geothermal energy taps into the natural heat beneath Earth's surface to produce power.

questions.question: Which renewable source is most reliable regardless of weather?
questions.explanation: Geothermal is constant—it doesn't depend on weather like solar or wind.

questions.question: What does "net metering" allow solar panel users to do?

answers.text: Sell extra electricity to the grid

questions.explanation: Net metering allows users to earn credit or money for excess power they generate.

questions.question: Which material is most used in solar cells?
questions.explanation: Silicon is a semiconductor widely used in photovoltaic (solar) cells for energy conversion.

questions.question: Which is a benefit of renewable energy?
questions.explanation: Renewable energy sources like solar and wind produce electricity without harmful emissions.

quizzes.title: SDG 13: Climate Action
quizzes.description: Understanding the United Nations Sustainable Development Goal 13 and climate action initiatives
quizzes.author: e-icon World Contest

questions.question: What is the aim of SDG 13?
questions.explanation: SDG 13 is focused on urgent action to address climate change and its impacts globally.

questions.question: When was the Paris Agreement signed?
questions.explanation: The Paris Agreement was adopted in 2015 to strengthen the global response to climate change.

questions.question: What is the key goal of the Paris Agreement?
questions.explanation: The agreement seeks to limit warming to well below 2°C, ideally 1.5°C, above pre-industrial levels.

questions.question: Which group is most responsible for implementing SDG 13?
questions.explanation: Governments must create and enforce policies to reduce emissions and prepare for climate impacts.

questions.question: What is the Green Climate Fund?

answers.text: International climate finance for developing countries

questions.explanation: It helps poorer countries build resilience and shift to low-emission development paths.

questions.question: What is "adaptation" in climate policy?
questions.explanation: Adaptation means preparing for climate impacts—like sea walls, drought-resistant crops, etc.

questions.question: Which action supports SDG 13 personally?
questions.explanation: Reducing electricity use lowers emissions and supports sustainability goals.

questions.question: What are NDCs in climate talks?
questions.explanation: NDCs are emission reduction plans that countries commit to under the Paris Agreement.

questions.question: Which global body oversees the SDGs?
questions.explanation: The UN developed and monitors the 17 Sustainable Development Goals, including SDG 13.

questions.question: What is "loss and damage" in climate negotiations?

answers.text: Compensation for climate harm in vulnerable countries

questions.explanation: "Loss and damage" refers to funding and support for countries facing irreversible climate impacts.
